hints.content:
The graph of $y=\sqrt[3]{x}$ can be transformed
to get the graph of $y=2\sqrt[3]{x-4}$. 
[[☃ explanation 1]]

options.explanation:
Suppose $f(x)=\sqrt[3]{x}$ and $g(x)=2\sqrt[3]{x-4}$.  

>$\begin{align}f(x)&=\sqrt[3]{x}\\\\
f(x-4)&=\sqrt[3]{x-4}\\\\
2f(x-4)&=2\sqrt[3]{x-4}\\\\
\end{align}$

Notice that what is on the right-hand side of the equal sign is $g(x)$.  Therefore, $g(x)=2f(x-4)$.  

Since function $g$ can be built from function $f$, the graph of function $g$ is a transformation of the graph of function $f$.

hints.content:
Replacing $x$ with $x-4$ shifts the graph of $y=\sqrt[3]{x}$ right $4$ units.

[[☃ image 1]]

options.alt: A cube root function graph and its shifted graph on an x y coordinate plane. It has a middle point at (zero, zero) and passes through (negative eight, negative two) and (eight, two). The shifted graph has a middle point at (four, zero) and passes through (negative four, negative two) and (twelve, two).

hints.content:
Multiplying $\sqrt[3]{x-4}$ by $2$ stretches the graph of $y=\sqrt[3]{x-4} $ vertically by a factor of $2$.  

[[☃ image 1]]

Note that the graph of the function passes through $(-4,-2)$ *before* the stretch, and $(-4, -4 )$ *after* the stretch.  This is because each $y$-coordinate is multiplied by $2$.  

Additionally it is important to follow order of operations when building the function, as function transformations are not always commutative.  [[☃ explanation 1]]

options.explanation:
Consider the graph of $y=\sqrt{x}$.

If we shift the graph of $y=\sqrt{x}$ down $2$ units, and then reflect this across the $x$-axis, we get the following graph.

![A square root function graph on an x y coordinate plane. It has an endpoint (zero, two) and passes through (ten, negative one).](web+graphie:${☣ LOCALPATH}/images/838d19b306cd3a25ac6c67be671bb6a26eaf0e71)

However, if we first reflect the graph of $y=\sqrt{x}$ across the $x$-axis and then shift this graph down $2$ units, we get the following graph.

![A square root function graph on an x y coordinate plane. It has an endpoint (zero, negative two) and passes through (ten, negative five).](web+graphie:${☣ LOCALPATH}/images/76bbee52d28bfb5f5bcd72a6831a797eaab9824d)

These graphs are not the same, indicating that the order in which you perform the transformations is important!

options.alt: A cube root function graph and its stretched graph on an x y coordinate plane. It has a middle point at (four, zero) and passes through (negative four, negative two) and (twelve, two). The stretched graph has a middle point at (four, zero) and passes through (negative four, negative four) and (twelve, four).
